title: Musa and the shepherd
hook: Musa rebukes a shepherd's simple prayer, and is told Allah looks at the heart, not the words (Masnavi 2)
tomorrow: everyone's touching the same elephant. why do they disagree?

segments.voice: Last week ended with a parrot playing dead to get out of its cage: let the part that keeps you caged go quiet. Die before dying. This week opens on a hillside.
screen: `DIE BEFORE DYING.` → `A NEW WEEK, A HILLSIDE.`

segments.voice: Bedtime, and a little kid squeezes his eyes shut: dear God, thanks for my dog, and for pizza, and please fix Grandma's knee, and do You have a dog? The grown-ups in the doorway try not to laugh. Rumi tells a story about a prayer like that. A shepherd sits on a hillside, talking out loud to God: where are You, so I can sew Your shoes and comb Your hair, wash Your clothes, bring You milk, kiss Your hands? And a prophet is walking by and hears every word. It's Musa, Moses. He stops. He's horrified.
screen: `DO YOU HAVE A DOG?` → `I'LL SEW YOUR SHOES.` → `MUSA HEARS EVERY WORD.`

segments.voice: Musa rounds on the shepherd. Who are you talking to? God has no body; He needs no milk and no shoes. Talk like that is an insult. The shepherd tears his shirt in shame and runs off into the desert. Then the revelation comes to Musa, and it's a rebuke. Paraphrased: you have separated My servant from Me. You were sent to bring people together, not to cut them off. I don't look at the tongue and the words; I look at the heart and its state. Musa runs after the shepherd, finds him, and tells him: there are no rules for you. Say whatever your heart says. Here's what makes the story more than sweet. Musa wasn't wrong about God. The Qur'an itself says there is nothing like Him. His theology was right, and his timing and tone cut a man off from God. The story keeps both: right belief matters, and correction must never sever. Its center has a hadith behind it, in Sahih Muslim: God does not look at your bodies or your appearance, but at your hearts and your deeds. The shepherd's words were clumsy. His heart was burning. He looks at the heart.
screen: `MUSA: GOD NEEDS NO SHOES.` · `SENT TO UNITE, NOT TO CUT OFF.` · `RIGHT BELIEF, GENTLE CORRECTION.` · `HEARTS AND DEEDS, NOT FORMS.` · then, large: `HE LOOKS AT THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Say one sentence out loud in the plainest words you own, no polish, no special language. If you pray, say it to God the way the shepherd did, as if to someone close; if not, say aloud one plain thing you're grateful for. Then sit with how it felt to say it simply.
Musa and the shepherd: Rumi's story of a prophet who corrects a clumsy prayer and is told God looks at the heart.
For the clumsy prayers, yours and other people's: He looks at the heart. Four of Rumi's eight stories now.

screen: `DAY 1632 COUNTS.` → `RUMI'S MASNAVI · 4 OF 8.` → `TOMORROW: WHY DOES EVERYONE DISAGREE ABOUT THE ELEPHANT?`

howItsDone: Alongside the set words of the daily prayer, Muslims make dua, personal prayer, in any language and their own words; teachers use Musa and the shepherd to warn against shaming sincere but clumsy prayer.

myth: Rumi's story says correct belief about God doesn't matter
Musa was right that God has no body. the rebuke was for cutting the shepherd off.
a hadith in Sahih Muslim says God looks at your hearts and deeds, not your bodies or appearance
it stands behind the story's center: He looks at the heart.

fork.setup: after the masjid's kids' class, a little boy tells you God has a big white beard and lives on a cloud. his mom is nearby. what fits Musa's story?
options: smile, take his question seriously, and leave gentle teaching for later.
correct him right away so the wrong picture doesn't stick.
tell him anything he believes is fine, since only the heart counts.
fork.reveal: the story keeps both halves: right belief matters, and correction must never cut someone off from God. Musa was sent to unite.

original.note: Arabic: heart; in the hadith, the place God looks.

trapdoor: what you thought: any words to God are fine, and theology doesn't matter.
what it means: a burning heart in clumsy words is heard, and correcting someone must never cut them off from God.
what a scholar hears: Masnavi Book 2; Musa's theology matches the Qur'an's 'nothing is like Him,' and the story's center echoes Sahih Muslim on hearts and deeds.
guess: sincere words from the heart reach God
only exact, formal words reach God
a prophet's prayers count more than others'

chat.says: my little cousin's dua at dinner: "thank u for fries." my aunt says he's doing it wrong. is he??
options: Not wrong. He looks at the heart, and that was honest. Teach him more later.
Yes; plain words don't count, so he should only use the Arabic duas.
Kids' prayers don't count yet, so it doesn't matter what he says.
chat.meaning: In Rumi's story, God tells Musa He looks at the heart, not the words, and that Musa was sent to unite, not to cut off.

Musa.meaning: Moses, a prophet in the Qur'an

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major hadith collection gathered by Imam Muslim

Rumi.meaning: a Persian poet and Sufi teacher of Konya
